title: On a video the Ask button never sits on top of the panel
goal: On a video in Edit, the Ask button lands on top of the right panel: it covers the Transitions search field, and once the panel scrolls, rows such as Intensity slide up underneath Ask and the View and Edit switch with nothing between them. A person reads two things on top of each other and cannot click the field under Ask. Ask, View and Edit should sit in a title bar strip of their own, and the panel's rows should start below it or pass under it the way content passes under a Mac toolbar.
notes: Reproduced by the manager 2026-10-20 08:16: Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build ask-adds-a-title-page passed, and its pictures /tmp/photonz-playtest/ask-adds-a-title-page-walk/1-plan-sc.png and 2-ran-sc.png show the overlap (crops saved under queue/manager/shots/). The Ask button came with 8238a30a: Sources/Photonz/TitlebarPanelToggle.swift:147-156 widens the right slot by AskTitlebarButton.width when offersAsk; AskTitlebarButton in Sources/Photonz/Agent/AskViews.swift:11. On a video the panel runs to the window top (the View and Edit switch already floated over it before Ask); on a picture Layers starts below the title bar. Placement contract: the title bar row (docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md, line 24 and section 1 line 322) owns Ask, the mode and the panel toggle; the panel starts under it. Check whether the video panel's top inset counts the wider right slot.
acceptance: Reproduce first with ask-adds-a-title-page-walk at Next defaults: its plan shot shows Ask over the Transitions search field, its ran shot shows the Intensity row under Ask and View and Edit (queue/manager/shots/2026-10-20-video-ask-over-panel-search.png and 2026-10-20-video-ask-over-panel-rows.png)

Scrolled panel content passes under the title bar the way it does on a picture, with the same edge treatment, never as text drawn straight under the buttons
A walk proves it: it scrolls the panel on a video and checks that no panel control's frame meets the title bar controls' frames, and that the Transitions search field takes a click
Pictures, icons and designs are unchanged (photograph a picture's title bar before and after)
